newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-HILL LEADS PISTONS WITH NINTH TRIPLE DOUBLE OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-HILL LEADS PISTONS WITH NINTH TRIPLE DOUBLE OF SEASON.

text.p: Grant Hill recorded his 20th career triple-double and ninth of the season on Wednesday to lead the Detroit Pistons to a 99-92 victory over the San Antonio Spurs.
Hill had 31 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for his second triple-double in three games.
"Hopefully I can continue to improve and just get better and better," Hill said. "I try to be active and take what the defence gives me."
Otis Thorpe added 17 points and Joe Dumars 14, including three three-pointers in the fourth quarter for the Pistons.
Carl Herrera scored 22 points and Dominique Wilkins added 19 to lead the Spurs.
Dumars opened the fourth with a trey to spark a 10-2 run that put Detroit up 79-70 and the Pistons never looked back.
"It was a great game except for 1:30 of bad basketball on our part," San Antonio coach Gregg Popovich said of the pivotal fourth-quarter run by Detroit.
In Los Angeles, Eddie Jones scored 27 points to lead the injury-plagued Lakers to a 110-85 rout of the Denver Nuggets and into a tie with Seattle for first place in the Pacific Division.
Nick Van Exel added 18 points and 12 assists in the Lakers' fifth consecutive win.
Los Angeles played without Travis Knight and Elden Campbell, who were injured in Tuesday's win at Seattle, and without Shaquille O'Neal who has been sidelined for weeks with a serious knee injury.
Antonio McDyess led Denver with 21 points.
At Minnesota, Kevin Garnett scored 24 points and sank a key jumper down the stretch as the Timberwolves inched closer to a playoff berth with a 94-89 win over the New Jersey Nets.

Tom Gugliotta and Stephon Marbury each had 21 points and nine assists for the Timberwolves (36-37), who are on the verge of qualifying for post season for the first time since entering the NBA in 1989.
Kendall Gill scored 23 points and Jim Jackson added 22 for the Nets, who will not make the playoffs.
"I think Marbury is Rookie of the Year," Gill said. "He runs the offence. He makes big shots and he plays defence."

At Utah, Karl Malone and Bryon Russell led a furious first-half charge as the Jazz opened a whopping 39-point halftime lead and cruised to their 10th straight win, a 118-87 victory over the Sacramento Kings.
Malone scored 15 of his 23 points in the first half, when the Jazz shot a blistering 59.5 percent (25-of-42) from the field en route to a 67-28 halftime advantage.
Russell scored 13 of his 19 points in the first quarter, including five in a 17-2 burst that turned a tie game into a 26-11 lead. The Jazz led 36-18 lead after one quarter.
Mitch Richmond scored 15 points for the Kings, who fell to 0-5 on their current road trip.

In Phoenix, Kevin Johnson had 30 points and 12 assists and Wesley Person scored seven of his 21 in a 12-0 run to close the third quarter as the surging Suns posted a 109-96 victory over the Houston Rockets.
The Suns' seventh successive win and 10th in 11 games spoiled the return to Phoenix of Houston's Charles Barkley.

Hakeem Olajuwon scored 33 points and Clyde Drexler added 20 for the Rockets. But Barkley, who sat out 14 games with a hip injury, missed his first 12 shots against his former club and finished with just six points. He did grab 16 rebounds.
In Charlotte, Glen Rice poured in 38 points, including 11 in the fourth quarter as the Hornets snapped Atlanta's seven-game winning streak with a 95-84 victory over the Hawks.
Ricky Pierce added 16 points and Muggsy Bogues 12 and nine assists for Charlotte, which held Atlanta to 15 points in the third quarter.
Steve Smith scored 25 points and Christian Laettner added 23 and nine rebounds for the Hawks, who fell back to fifth place in the Eastern Conference, one game behind Detroit.
In Boston, Chris Mills scored 24 points and Tyrone Hill bounced back from a sub-par effort with 19 points and 11 rebounds to lead the Cleveland Cavaliers to a 96-87 win over the woeful Celtics.
Hill, who was held to just two points in Tuesday's loss to the Knicks, sparked a pivotal 13-0 second-half run with a layup to end the third quarter.
Antoine Walker scored 25 points to lead Boston, which has dropped 28 of its last 30 games.
In Philadelphia, Doug Christie scored 12 of his 29 points in a 40-point fourth quarter as the Toronto Raptors raced to a 112-90 victory over the 76ers.
Carlos Rogers had 24 points and 13 rebounds and Damon Stoudamire added 23 points and 15 assists for the Raptors. Christie also pulled down 15 boards as Toronto out-rebounded the Sixers 57-35.
Jerry Stackhouse scored 36 points and Allen Iverson added 22 for the 76ers, whose three-game winning streak was halted.
